section: Bhakti in Andhra - Annamacharya, Bammera Potana, Vemana, the Tallapaka poets
subsections: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage
Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja

accepted.s: Bammera Potana, the author of Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, belonged to which of the following periods?
accepted.x: Bammera Potana lived approximately from 1450 to 1510.
accepted.tq: Use the middle-value year trap while distinguishing closely placed periods.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Bammera, the native place of Potana, is associated with which present district?
accepted.x: Potana was a native of Bammera in present-day Janagama district of Telangana.
accepted.tq: Test the precise birthplace rather than the broader regional identity.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs of titles is associated with Bammera Potana?
accepted.x: Potana was known by the titles Sahaja Panditudu and Nigarva Chudamani.
accepted.tq: Use exact title-pair recognition to eliminate titles belonging to other poets.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Veerabhadra Vijayam was written by Potana for whom?
accepted.x: Potana wrote his first work, Veerabhadra Vijayam, for his guru Ivaturi Somanaradhyudu.
accepted.tq: Apply the author–dedicatee distinction instead of confusing a guru with a royal patron.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s:
With reference to Potana’s Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu, consider the following statements:
1. It is the Telugu version of the Bhagavata Purana.
2. Potana dedicated it to Lord Rama.
3. Potana wrote all the twelve skandhas.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu is the Telugu Bhagavata Purana and was offered to Lord Rama. Potana wrote eight of its twelve skandhas, not all twelve.
accepted.tq: Find the overstatement in the claim that one author completed the entire work.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: How many skandhas of Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu were written by Potana?
accepted.x: Potana wrote eight of the twelve skandhas of Andhra Maha Bhagavatamu.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the author’s actual share from the total number of skandhas.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Veligandala Narayana — Eleventh and twelfth skandhas
accepted.x: The eleventh and twelfth skandhas were written by Veligandala Narayana. Potana wrote eight skandhas, while the fifth and sixth were written by Bopparaju Gangana and Erchuri Singana respectively.
accepted.tq: Find the wrongly assigned contributor in a list of author–section pairs.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Which work of Potana is described as the first independent Dandakam in Telugu?
accepted.x: Bhogini Dandakam is regarded as the first independent Dandakam in Telugu.
accepted.tq: Match the superlative description with the exact literary work.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Bhogini Dandakam deals with which of the following?
accepted.x: Bhogini Dandakam is associated with Sarvajna Singabhupala and Bhogini.
accepted.tq: Use the work–subject association to distinguish similar devotional themes.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Which one of the following works of Potana is described as lost?
accepted.x: Narayana Satakam is listed as a lost work of Potana.
accepted.tq: Test the exceptional status in a list of surviving works.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Who printed the Bhagavatamu in 1840?
accepted.x: C. P. Brown printed the Bhagavatamu in 1840.
accepted.tq: Combine the publication year with the correct editor-printer identity.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s:
Potana’s refusal to dedicate his Bhagavatamu to a human king primarily reflects his:
1. Refusal to dedicate the work to Sarvajna Singabhupala.
2. Dedication of the work to Sri Rama.
3. Dependence on royal patronage as the central principle of his literary outlook.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Potana refused to dedicate the work to Sarvajna Singabhupala and offered it to Sri Rama. This represents independence from, rather than dependence on, royal patronage.
accepted.tq: Reject the reversed interpretation of a poet’s refusal of royal patronage.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Potana is described as a contemporary of which poet?
accepted.x: Potana was a contemporary of Srinatha.
accepted.tq: Use the contemporary-pair relationship rather than the literary work association.
accepted.sec: Bammera Potana → works and attitude to royal patronage

accepted.s: Kshetrayya was primarily associated with which deity?
accepted.x: Kshetrayya composed Shringara padams dedicated to Muvva Gopala, a form of Krishna.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the deity associated with each Andhra bhakti poet.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Kshetrayya’s association with Muvva refers to which present location?
accepted.x: Kshetrayya, also known as Varadayya, came from Muvva or Movva in Krishna district.
accepted.tq: Test the exact regional location of a poet’s place-name association.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which literary form is especially associated with Kshetrayya?
accepted.x: Kshetrayya is known for his Shringara padams, including the Movva Gopala padams.
accepted.tq: Match the poet with the distinctive literary genre rather than the deity alone.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which statement regarding Kshetrayya is correct?
o: He composed over a thousand Movva Gopala padams at Abdullah Qutb Shah’s court.
He wrote the Basava Puranam in Dwipada metre at the Kakatiya court.
He composed the Pancharatna kritis at Tiruvaiyaru.
accepted.x: Kshetrayya composed over a thousand Movva Gopala padams and is associated with Abdullah Qutb Shah’s court.
accepted.tq: Use the court–composer–work combination to separate closely related bhakti figures.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Bhakta Ramadasu:
1. He served as a Golconda revenue official under Tana Shah.
2. He built the Bhadrachalam temple.
3. He was jailed in connection with the construction of the temple.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Ramadasu, or Kancharla Gopanna, served under Tana Shah, built the Bhadrachalam temple and was imprisoned for it.
accepted.tq: Verify a complete chain of office, religious construction and punishment.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Tyagaraja’s compositions are predominantly devoted to:
accepted.x: Tyagaraja composed Telugu kritis predominantly in devotion to Rama.
accepted.tq: Separate the principal deity of Tyagaraja from those of other Telugu bhakti poets.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the members of the Carnatic Trinity other than Tyagaraja?
accepted.x: The Carnatic Trinity consists of Tyagaraja, Muthuswami Dikshitar and Syama Sastri.
accepted.tq: Complete a well-defined triad by identifying the two associated names.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Annamacharya composed Sankirtanas on Venkateswara of Tirumala. Vemana is associated with Vemana padyalu, Tyagaraja with kritis, and Pedda Tirumalacharya with Venkateshwara Satakam.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure poet–work association and eliminate the swapped pairs.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Annamacharya is popularly known by which title?
accepted.x: Tallapaka Annamacharya is known as the Padakavita Pitamaha.
accepted.tq: Distinguish honorific titles among contemporary Telugu poets.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who wrote Venkateshwara Satakam?
accepted.x: Pedda Tirumalacharya, one of the Tallapaka poets, wrote Venkateshwara Satakam.
accepted.tq: Apply the author–work pair without confusing members of the Tallapaka family.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Vemana’s poetry is notable for its strong condemnation of:
accepted.x: Vemana strongly condemned caste and expressed his views through Vemana padyalu.
accepted.tq: Identify the social reform theme attached to the poet’s verses.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Dhurjati is associated with which work?
accepted.x: Dhurjati wrote Srikalahasteeswara Satakam, regarded as a foremost Shaiva satakam.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similarly named satakams by their author and deity.
accepted.sec: Other Andhra bhakti figures - Kshetrayya, Ramadasu, Tyagaraja  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Virashaivism was founded by Basaveswara in:
o: Tamil Nadu in the thirteenth century
accepted.x: Basaveswara founded Virashaivism in Karnataka during the twelfth century.
accepted.tq: Combine the correct region and century while rejecting shifted locations and dates.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who is credited with introducing Virashaivism into Andhra?
accepted.x: Virashaivism entered Andhra through Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya, after which Pandita reformers helped spread it.
accepted.tq: Separate the figure who introduced a movement from the later literary propagator.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Palkuriki Somanatha spread Basava’s teachings in Telugu primarily through:
accepted.x: Palkuriki Somanatha spread Basava’s teachings through Basava Puranam, written in Telugu.
accepted.tq: Match the reformer with the principal vehicle of his teachings.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Basava Puranam of Palkuriki Somanatha was written in which metre?
accepted.x: Basava Puranam was written in the simple Telugu Dwipada metre.
accepted.tq: Test the precise literary form rather than the broad language of composition.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a work of Palkuriki Somanatha?
accepted.x: Sivatattvasaram was written by Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya. Basava Puranam, Panditaradhya Charitra and Basavana Ragada are associated with Palkuriki Somanatha.
accepted.tq: Find the work belonging to the neighbouring author in a closely related literary group.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Palkuriki Somanatha’s Desi kavita was characterised by the use of:
o: Simple native metres such as Dwipada, Ragada, Manjari and Kanda
accepted.x: Somanatha championed Desi kavita, using simple native metres such as Dwipada, Ragada, Manjari and Kanda against the Sanskritised Marga style.
accepted.tq: Use the contrast between Desi and Marga to identify the inclusive list of metres.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who wrote Sivatattvasaram, comprising about 400 kanda poems?
accepted.x: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya wrote Sivatattvasaram, which contains about 400 kanda poems.
accepted.tq: Use the distinctive numerical detail to identify the correct author.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya is regarded as the originator of which literary form in Telugu?
accepted.x: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya is regarded as the originator of the Sataka form in Telugu.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the originator of a literary form from poets associated with individual examples.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes Aradhya Saivism?
o: A Vaishnava sect centred exclusively on Venkateswara worship
A radical sect that rejected Vedic learning and varna distinctions
A court tradition that opposed all forms of devotional worship
A moderate Andhra Shaiva sect that retained Vedic learning and varna while preaching Shiva bhakti
accepted.x: Aradhya Saivism was the moderate Andhra Shaiva tradition associated with Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya; it retained Vedic learning and varna while preaching devotion to Shiva.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a moderate reform tradition from an incorrectly exaggerated radical description.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT among the teachings associated with the Virashaiva tradition described in Andhra?
accepted.x: The teachings emphasised equality, devotion to Shiva, dignity of labour and opposition to caste discrimination; compulsory caste hierarchy is contrary to them.
accepted.tq: Identify the statement that reverses the movement’s social message.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Vrushadhipa Satakam is significant because it is regarded as:
o: The first Telugu translation of the Bhagavata Purana
The first Telugu satakam with all satakam features
The first collection of Pancharatna kritis
accepted.x: Vrushadhipa Satakam, associated with Palkuriki Somanatha, is regarded as the first Telugu satakam possessing all satakam features.
accepted.tq: Match the distinctive literary distinction with the correct work.
accepted.sec: Kannada-Telugu Virashaiva links - Palkuriki Somanatha  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Tirumala — Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family
accepted.x: Tirumala is associated with Annamacharya and the Tallapaka family. Bhadrachalam is associated with Ramadasu, Muvva with Kshetrayya, and Srikurmam with Narahari Tirtha.
accepted.tq: Start from the temple–saint pair that is most firmly associated and eliminate shifted pairings.
accepted.sec: Temple → saint

accepted.s: Tarigonda Vengamamba is associated with which sacred place?
accepted.x: Tarigonda Vengamamba is included among the saints associated with Tirumala and the Venkateswara tradition.
accepted.tq: Test the less prominent name in a temple–saint association list.
accepted.sec: Temple → saint

accepted.s: Narahari Tirtha, associated with Srikurmam, is remembered for spreading:
accepted.x: Narahari Tirtha is associated with Srikurmam and spread the Dvaita tradition.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the philosophical affiliation from the nearby Shaiva traditions.
accepted.sec: Temple → saint

accepted.s:
Arrange the following associations in the order in which they appear from the temple–saint list:
A. Srikurmam — Narahari Tirtha
B. Tirumala — Annamacharya
C. Bhadrachalam — Bhakta Ramadasu
D. Muvva — Kshetrayya
accepted.x: The listed sequence is Tirumala–Annamacharya, Bhadrachalam–Ramadasu, Muvva–Kshetrayya and Srikurmam–Narahari Tirtha.
accepted.tq: Follow the first-and-last positions while preserving the sequence of a supplied association list.
accepted.sec: Temple → saint
